## Remote sensing of nutrient dynamics

::: {.thrust}
![](images/research-remote-sensing.jpg)

::: {}
[UAV hyperspectral · Satellite time series · Watershed nutrient monitoring]{.thrust-meta}

Nutrient monitoring at the watershed or landscape scale is critical for understanding ecosystem dynamics and ensuring envirnmental quality. My work uses satellite and drone (UAV) based sensor platforms to quantify, monitor, and predict nutrient dynamics at scale. 

:::
:::

## Interpretable machine learning

::: {.thrust}
![](images/research-interpretable-ml.jpg)

::: {}
[SHAP · Spatial cross-validation · Crop yield and soil quality prediction]{.thrust-meta}

Machine learning makes high dimensional data useful, but has a reputation as a "black box" technology - we cannot always explain how it makes the predictions it does. For many environmental challenges and systems, prediction accuracy alone is not not enough. We use interpretability methods (also known as "explainable AI" or XAI) to improve our understanding of the underlying system.
:::
:::

## Geospatial modeling of land suitability

::: {.thrust}
![](images/research-suitability.jpg)

::: {}
[Species distribution models · MaxEnt · Soil and climate suitability]{.thrust-meta}

Understanding what makes a particular piece of land suitable for a specific use is a complex question that involves multiple environmental factors. I use species distribution models an advanced geospatial techniques to identify what factors will lead to the best outcomes, so we can match land with it's ideal use case.
:::
:::
